Read and write Lucid pathway (dichotomous) keys

Source: R/lucid.R
readLucidKey.Rd

The Lucid Builder also makes "pathway" keys: ordinary dichotomous keys of couplets and leads (the successor of the stand-alone Lucid Phoenix). readLucidKey() reads one of its exports into a dimoose key and writeLucidKey() writes a dimoose key in the same forms. All four are described in the Lucid Builder help ("Pathway key exports"):

Usage

readLucidKey(file, format = NULL, desc = NULL)

writeLucidKey(key, file, format = c("lpxk", "csv", "text", "sdd"))

Arguments

file

Path of the file to read or write.

format

"lpxk", "csv", "text" or "sdd"; when reading, by default worked out from the file.

desc

Title of the key; by default the title in the file, if any.

key

A dimoose key.

Value

readLucidKey() returns a dimoose key; writeLucidKey() returns file, invisibly.

Details

  • "lpxk", Lucid Phoenix XML: <PhoenixKey> with the taxa as <Identity> elements and the couplets as <Step> elements holding <Lead>s whose goto names the next step or the taxon. The step's text becomes the couplet's Question, an identity's url the TaxonUrl. Filters (<FilterItem>) and icons are not read or written.

  • "csv": one line per lead, couplet,"lead text",next couplet or taxon.

  • "text": the same with blanks instead of commas, as printed in a paper.

  • "sdd": SDD with an identification key; see readSDDKey().

In the CSV and text forms the last field is read as a couplet when it matches a couplet number and as a taxon otherwise, so writeLucidKey() refuses to write a key in which a taxon is named like a couplet. These two forms hold neither the title of the key nor questions, links or images. The CSV, text and Phoenix XML forms follow the examples printed in the Lucid help; no file exported by the Lucid Builder itself was available to check them against, and no file written by dimoose has been imported into the Builder.

References

Lucid Builder help, "Pathway key exports", https://help.lucidcentral.org/lucid/pathway-key-exports/.

See also

readLucid() for Lucid matrix keys, readSDDKey(), keyFromSpreadsheet().

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "tdwg", "insects.lpxk", package = "dimoose")
k <- readLucidKey(f)
k
#> <dimoose key> Some orders of insects
#>   4 couplets, 8 leads, 5 taxa, up to 3 steps deep (2.4 on average)
k$leads[, c("Statement", "Choice", "Character", "Next", "Taxon")]
#>   Statement Choice                                                  Character
#> 1         1      a                                               Wings absent
#> 2         1      b                                              Wings present
#> 3         2      a     Body flattened from side to side, 1-2 mm long; jumping
#> 4         2      b Body flattened from above, 10-15 mm long, with three tails
#> 5         3      a                                       Forewings membranous
#> 6         3      b         Forewings hard covers that meet in a straight line
#> 7         4      a                           Hindwings reduced to small knobs
#> 8         4      b      Hindwings present; wings and body covered with scales
#>   Next        Taxon
#> 1    2             
#> 2    3             
#> 3    - Siphonaptera
#> 4    -    Zygentoma
#> 5    4             
#> 6    -   Coleoptera
#> 7    -      Diptera
#> 8    -  Lepidoptera

out <- writeLucidKey(k, tempfile(fileext = ".csv"), format = "csv")
readLines(out)
#> [1] "1,\"Wings absent\",2"                                                      
#> [2] "1,\"Wings present\",3"                                                     
#> [3] "2,\"Body flattened from side to side, 1-2 mm long; jumping\",Siphonaptera" 
#> [4] "2,\"Body flattened from above, 10-15 mm long, with three tails\",Zygentoma"
#> [5] "3,\"Forewings membranous\",4"                                              
#> [6] "3,\"Forewings hard covers that meet in a straight line\",Coleoptera"       
#> [7] "4,\"Hindwings reduced to small knobs\",Diptera"                            
#> [8] "4,\"Hindwings present; wings and body covered with scales\",Lepidoptera"
